channel.description: Recent content in Research news on Jinhee Kim

item.title: New research grant: Social disconnection
item.description: 2026–2031 · Principal Investigator · KRW 500 million I received a five-year grant from the National Research Foundation of Korea to study social disconnection. The project combines neuroimaging with repeated assessments of everyday experience to develop prediction models and interventions informed by brain and behavior.

item.title: Research grant: Interoception and social decision-making
item.description: 2023–2026 · Principal Investigator · KRW 210 million I received funding from the National Research Foundation of Korea to investigate how bodily signals influence social decision-making. This project combines neuroimaging and physiological measures to examine the role of interoception in how people respond to social feedback.

item.title: Research grant: Social decision-making in depression
item.description: 2020–2023 · Principal Investigator · KRW 195 million Supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea, this project examined how depression relates to the way people process social information and make decisions, using neuroimaging and non-invasive brain stimulation.

item.title: Awarded the Jaeil Kim Young Scholar Award
item.description: Jinhee Kim has been awarded the Kim Jae-Ill Young Investigator Paper Award by the Korean Psychological Association. The award recognizes outstanding research contributions by early-career scholars in psychology.

item.title: The CAMH Discovery Fund
item.description: I received a postdoctoral fellowship awarded by the Discovery Fund Talent Development Competition.

item.title: Mimi and Charles Hollenberg Research Award
item.description: I won an award at the annual Mimi and Charles Hollenberg Research Competition of the Department of Medicine of Mount Sinai Hospital and the University Health Network (the second prize for Category 4. Reports of research projects of a mechanistic mature).
